claude_code.supported_min_source: the .claude-plugin/marketplace.json schema this catalog ships has been stable since 2.0.0; the previous floor was never validated
claude_code.verification_method:
Live-CLI revalidation on 2026-10-31 -- `claude --version` on this run's runner reports `2.1.316 (Claude Code)`, newer than the official changelog's newest published entry (`2.1.312`, dated 2026-10-27). Per this review's instruction the changelog is the compatibility target, not a possibly-ahead local binary, so `validated_against` and `latest_known` both advance from 2.1.307 to **2.1.312** (five releases), while the live commands below still ran for real on the newer installed CLI. Reviewed the full 2.1.308-2.1.312 changelog for catalog surface: 2.1.308 is bug-fixes-and-reliability-improvements only, no itemized entries. 2.1.309 stopped worktree creation/reuse fetching objects on demand in ordinary clones, denied dangerous `rm`/`rmdir` instantly in bypass-permissions unattended sessions, made `sed -i` a real Bash edit action rather than a simulated preview, added a sandbox write-list ask when sandboxing can't run, and required workspace trust for `claude ultrareview` -- worktree-hook/CLI-execution surface, not a marketplace concern. 2.1.310 extended the `Monitor` tool to Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry, added cloud-session custom-role gating, and clarified MCP elicitation timeout errors -- no catalog surface, and no `.mcp.json` here to elicit anything. 2.1.311 made `DISABLE_COMPACT` one-way, dropped the `[1m]` model-name suffix label, and escaped control characters in `--output-format json`/`stream-json` output -- mod-dev/CLI surface this manifest-only catalog has none of. 2.1.312 fixed a subagent's `autoCompactWindow` not lowering a session-level `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW`, and raised the prompt/agent hook concurrency cap 12 -> 24 -- this catalog ships no subagent definitions and no hooks of its own, so neither applies. None of 2.1.308-2.1.312 touches a marketplace manifest or `.agents/skills` frontmatter. `claude plugin validate --strict .` (the Claude manifest), `make validate-skills` (`claude plugin validate --strict --json .agents/skills`), `make validate` (`scripts/validate-marketplaces.py`), `bash scripts/check-agent-drift.sh .`, `bash scripts/check-feature-equivalence.sh .`, and `scripts/check-platform-targets.sh . --assert-current` were all re-run live against the 2.1.316 CLI. The assert-current run surfaced one finding: the README's Claude Code badge still read `2.1.306` -- the value `platform-targets.json` carried *before* the 2.1.307 cycle bumped `validated_against` without updating the badge. Confirmed via `git stash` that the drift predates this review; fixed the badge to `2.1.312` this cycle. Re-confirmed `tamirs-superpowers`' four gating hooks (`agent.spawn`, `prompt.submit`, `tool.call`, `session.compact`) still all carry `.catch(($, e, next) => next(e))`, now against that repo's own 2.1.312 cycle (`make test-mods`, 56/56 passing) -- the 2.1.299 gating-hooks finding remains resolved upstream.

Prior verification carried forward below.

Live-CLI revalidation on 2026-10-21 -- `claude --version` on this run's runner reports `2.1.307 (Claude Code)`. `validated_against` and `latest_known` both advance from 2.1.306 to **2.1.307** (one release). Reviewed the full 2.1.307 changelog for catalog surface: Added `/claude-api api-version`, a `claude_code.safety_event` OpenTelemetry event, a VSCode voice-dictation auto-stop notice, and `@claude review stop`/`off`/`pause` for Code Review subscriptions -- none touch a marketplace manifest. Changed items are VSCode-extension TLS/cert handling, a WebSearch-budget notice wording tweak, an `axScreenReader`/`CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER` settings-tier restriction, and two self-hosted-runner changes (checkout-hook timeout, cert filtering) -- this catalog has no VSCode extension, no `axScreenReader` setting, no Code Review subscription, and no self-hosted-runner config of its own. Of the 6 improvements, the one with a plausible catalog angle is "fork subagents launched together are now each told which launch is their own, so forks are much less likely to try to start each other's work" -- reviewed against `tamirs-superpowers`' one forked skill (`targeted-debug`, `context: fork`) and found not applicable: that skill is never launched alongside a sibling fork, so there is no "launched together" case for this fix to help with. The other five (unparseable-tool-call retry, faster browser sign-in, clearer web-search 403 reasons, faster first reply in cloud sessions behind a stuck desktop MCP server, faster Remote Control connect with large pasted images) are host-side reliability this catalog benefits from passively. Of the 26 unitemized bug fixes, the one worth flagging for a sibling repo is the fix for HTTP MCP tool calls being sent twice when the connection closed mid-call -- continues the same double-dispatch theme as 2.1.299's "MCP tool calls... sometimes failing, or running twice, when a background reconnect closed the connection" already reviewed in the 2.1.294-2.1.300 pass above; not actionable here since this manifest-only catalog defines no `.mcp.json` server, but directly relevant to `production-master-mcp`, which does. Re-ran `claude plugin validate --strict .` on the live 2.1.307 CLI: clean. `make validate` and `bash scripts/check-platform-targets.sh . --assert-current` both pass once `validated_against`/`latest_known` land on 2.1.307. Only Claude Code entries in this shared platform-target file were touched. Prior verification (2026-10-21, 2.1.306): Live-CLI revalidation on 2026-10-21 -- this run's runner has the `claude` CLI installed and `claude --version` reports `2.1.306 (Claude Code)`, matching the target exactly. `validated_against` and `latest_known` both advance from 2.1.300 to **2.1.306** together (no divergence), covering six releases (2.1.301-2.1.306). Reviewed every changelog entry across that range for catalog surface -- none required a `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (or generated `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` / `.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json`) schema change: 2.1.301-2.1.302 (`.catch` on a mod hook now runs only on throw or timeout, `$.env.set` resolves `{}`/`{ deny }`, at most 12 prompt/agent hooks of one event run concurrently, fork subagents default on, `-p`/SDK start in `default` permission mode on third-party/telemetry-off, MCP servers negotiating protocol 2026-07-28 without `resultType`/`ttlMs`/`cacheScope` no longer show no tools) is all mod-dev/CLI surface -- this catalog ships no `hooks.json`/`plugin.json`/`.mcp.json` of its own. 2.1.303 is bug fixes and reliability improvements only, with no itemized changelog entries. 2.1.304 (`/auto-mode-setup`, `decider: "person"` and `e.isReadOnly` on a mod's `tool.check` event, `/claude-api managed-agents-secure`, tool search on by default behind a custom `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, a cap of 1,024 hooks/16,384 matcher characters per skill source) is mod-dev/gateway surface with nothing to change here. 2.1.305 (`sandbox.allowNestedUserNamespaces`, `CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG_USAGE_LIMIT_RECHECK_MS`, a narrower `allowedMcpServers` filter for `managed-mcp.json`, an `/artifacts` delete-confirmation UX change) touches no marketplace manifest. 2.1.306 fixed `claude -p` in cloud sessions reporting "Not logged in" without the session's environment variables, and an API error being replaced by "prompt is too long" in sessions with many MCP tools -- host-side reliability fixes this catalog benefits from passively. Re-ran `claude plugin validate --strict .` against this catalog's own marketplace manifest on the live 2.1.306 CLI: clean, no warnings. `make validate` (regenerate + validate manifests, agent-drift, feature-equivalence, platform-targets, GitHub-Actions-SHA-pinning, `scripts/validate-marketplaces.py`) passes clean: 3 plugins in sync. `bash scripts/check-platform-targets.sh . --assert-current` passes once `validated_against`/`latest_known` both land on 2.1.306 (it failed with "Stale platform target claude_code" when only `latest_known` had been advanced, confirming the check actually fires). Cross-repo note: the gating-hooks finding escalated in this PR's Future opportunities since the 2.1.299 cycle ("`tamirs-superpowers`' mod has 4 gating hooks without a `.catch`") is now RESOLVED upstream -- `tamirs-superpowers` 5.0.0/5.0.1 added explicit `.catch(($, e, next) => next(e))` handlers to all four (`agent.spawn`, `prompt.submit`, `tool.call`, `session.compact`), confirmed live by that repo's own `claude plugin validate .claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `make test-mods` (56/56 passing) against the 2.1.306 CLI. No action needed here; the install guide, `docs/agent-guidelines/security.md`, and `docs/agent-guidelines/testing.md` are updated below to stop carrying the stale escalation. Only Claude Code entries in this shared platform-target file were touched; Cursor, Codex, and OpenCode values are untouched.

cursor.supported_min_source: Cursor documents no minimum version for plugins; the floor is the version actually validated rather than guessed. The previous 0.45.0 floor predates Cursor's plugin system entirely
cursor.verification_method: latest desktop build from official Cursor download links (3.18.9, 2026-08-30 stable) cross-checked against cursor.com/changelog (feature 3.11; date-only entries through 2026-09-02 Self-Hosted Machines / Team Pools / partner sandboxes / computer use); team-marketplace import is a Dashboard flow

codex.supported_min_source: earliest release this catalog has claimed .agents/plugins/marketplace.json support for
codex.verification_method: documentary revalidation by this repo's standing Codex method (official release notes plus catalog compatibility review; the Codex CLI is not installed on the review machine). Reviewed every openai/codex release from 0.148.0 through 0.153.4 for plugin/marketplace changes: #41208 (0.151.0) reports invalid project marketplaces without hiding valid plugins, #41953 (0.153.0) enforces a marketplace source policy for OpenAI-curated plugins only, and #42149/#42150 (0.153.0) upgrade Git marketplaces from merged configuration and add remote-marketplace support to the plugin CLI. None alter the portable Agent Plugin catalog shape, so .agents/plugins/marketplace.json remains discoverable unchanged; 0.153.0 widens how it can be consumed rather than narrowing it.

opencode.supported_min_source: oldest version on which `skills.paths` discovery of a catalog plugin's skills was verified with `opencode debug skill`
opencode.verification_method: `opencode --version` on the maintainer machine (reported 1.18.29); latest from registry.npmjs.org/opencode-ai. OpenCode has no marketplace, so the catalog itself cannot be installed — skill discovery is verified directly with `opencode debug skill`, pointing `skills.paths` at this repo's `.agents/skills` and confirming `run-plugins-catalog` resolves to its `SKILL.md`

capability_gaps.marketplace: OpenCode has no plugin marketplace and no plugin manifest, so this catalog cannot be added as an install source. Each plugin repo is installed directly — clone it and point `skills.paths` at its `skills/` directory, or symlink it into the OpenCode skills directory. Every plugin in this catalog ships its own `opencode.json` and its own OpenCode install guide.
capability_gaps.catalog_discovery: There is no OpenCode equivalent of listing plugins from a remote catalog. The plugin table in this repo's README is the discovery surface; installation is then per-repo.
